genie_retrieval_phase.retrieved_lesson_applied: A build-output governance violation and the coverage gap in the scanner meant to catch it are two independent failures -- closing only the data violation without also closing the scanner's blind spot leaves the same class of violation free to recur undetected.
genie_retrieval_phase.prediction_made_before_reading_relevant_: The fix would require finding and updating some tracking/allowlist mechanism that was never taught about the new files, not merely confirming the export files themselves exist on disk.

diagnosis_phase.initial_hypothesis_and_self_correction: First inspected project_governance/ACTIVE_ASSETS_REGISTRY.json, whose active_exports:[] looked like the obvious culprit. Before editing it, traced validateActiveExportVersionRule (services/projectGovernanceAudit.ts) to find its actual `entries` source: buildProjectInventory (services/projectInventoryBuilder.ts), which is driven by ASSET_LIFECYCLE_REGISTRY.json, a separate file -- not ACTIVE_ASSETS_REGISTRY.json, which is unused by this specific check. Corrected course before making any edit.
diagnosis_phase.root_cause: project_governance/ASSET_LIFECYCLE_REGISTRY.json (dated 2026-08-06, phase PHASE-PROJECT-GOVERNANCE-001) predates the exports/movie_spatial/{ACTIVE,TEST,MANUAL,ARCHIVE} export-root restructure (phase PHASE-PROJECT-GOVERNANCE-004, generationOutputPaths.ts). It lists the pre-restructure flat-path exports/movie_spatial/{titanic,spirited-away}-image-app-native-import-v8.json as LEGACY with replacement:null, and has no entry at all for the new exports/movie_spatial/ACTIVE/*-v8.json paths those files actually live at today. projectInventoryBuilder.ts's live filesystem walk (exports is a scanned root) discovers the new files but defaults any path absent from this lifecycle registry to status UNTRACKED, so validateActiveExportVersionRule's ACTIVE-status filter counted 0 for both movies despite the real, passing v8 exports existing on disk (confirmed separately via verify:generation-output-lock PASS).

repair_phase.change: Added exactly 2 new entries (status: ACTIVE, owner_phase: PHASE-PROJECT-GOVERNANCE-004) for exports/movie_spatial/ACTIVE/titanic-image-app-native-import-v8.json and exports/movie_spatial/ACTIVE/spirited-away-image-app-native-import-v8.json.
repair_phase.deliberately_not_changed: The existing LEGACY entries' replacement pointers, which all still point at the old flat-path v8 export (not the new ACTIVE path) -- a related but separate completeness gap, left out of this minimal fix.

verification.environment_note: Verified in the main working tree via npm run verify:project-governance. Fresh-worktree isolation for this specific verify script was not pursued: it separately depends on project_governance/PROJECT_GOVERNANCE_RULES.json, itself untracked and unrelated to this fix, and this task was explicitly scoped to real GENIE OJT work, not a return to persistence-gap hunting.

memory_effectiveness_assessment.how: The retrieved lesson correctly predicted the shape of the bug -- a tracking/allowlist mechanism never updated alongside a real change -- before any of this task's specific code was read, and directed the diagnosis toward finding a registry rather than merely re-confirming the export files exist. The specific mechanism differed from the retrieved record's own (ASSET_LIFECYCLE_REGISTRY.json here vs. outputLocationAudit.ts's IMAGE_APP_BUILDER_FILES scanner allowlist there) -- the retrieval surfaced a transferable diagnostic pattern, not a literally reusable fix.
memory_effectiveness_assessment.limitation_observed: 7 of the query phrasings tried (paraphrases closer to how the problem is described in English/governance terms) returned NOT_FOUND; only a phrasing close to the retrieved record's own vocabulary ("ACTIVE native import export") matched via the structural token-overlap fallback. Literal/structural retrieval remains sensitive to query wording even when a genuinely relevant record exists in the corpus.
